Top News
 
 
 
 
HABesen/iStock Editorial via Getty Images
 
 
 Wall Street ended the week in the green, as investors digested blockbuster Nvidia ( NVDA ) earnings, policy signals from the Jackson Hole symposium, and the latest U.S. GDP print.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) took center stage, reporting Q2 revenue of $96.2B, a 106% year-over-year increase. The chipmaker also offered an impressive forecast of 70% revenue growth for next year, citing massive AI infrastructure spending and broad-based demand. 

At the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh vowed to bring inflation down to the central bank's 2% target while discussing the economic impacts of artificial intelligence and emphasizing the need for a "quieter Fed." 

On the economic data front, the updated U.S. GDP print showed that real GDP increased by 1.5% annualized from Q1 to Q2 2026. 

The blue-chip Dow ( DJI ) climbed +0.5% this week, while the benchmark S&P ( SP500 ) also gained +0.5% , and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( COMP:IND ) rose +0.9% .

Read a preview of next week's major events in Seeking Alpha's Catalyst Watch. 


 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Outlook
 
 
 
 Retiree benefits 
 
 
 
Seeking Alpha
 
 
Social Security's trust fund is expected to run out of money by 2031, after which an automatic 22% benefit cut will get triggered – unless Congress acts.  Americans retiring this decade are projected to collect more than triple the amount that they put into the program, the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget noted. While the CRFB doesn't use generational framing, it's clear that Baby Boomers are reaping these benefits, while younger generations foot the bill. Read more.

 RTX : Premium Price Tag, Growth Prospects Priced In .

 SCHD's  Stunning Outperformance Even Startled Me .

Salesforce ( CRM ) Rewarded The Brave, Time To Sell .

 TLT : AI Productivity Gains Threaten Long-End Treasuries .
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Weekly Movement
 
 
 
 U.S. Indices 
Dow +0.5% to 53,560. S&P 500 +0.5% to 7,712. Nasdaq +0.9% to 26,402. Russell 2000 -1.5% to 2,972. CBOE Volatility Index -4.6% to 14.43. 

 S&P 500 Sectors 
Consumer Staples -0.5% . Utilities -0.2% . Financials +1.1% . Telecom +1.6% . Healthcare -2% . Industrials -1.7% . Information Technology +1.8% . Materials -0.4% . Energy -2% . Consumer Discretionary +0.1% . Real Estate -1.3% . 

 World Indices 
London +0.1% to 10,824. France -1% to 8,401. Germany +1.7% to 26,570. Japan +0.6% to 66,406. China +1.2% to 3,952. Hong Kong -1.6% to 25,585. India -0.4% to 77,265. 

 Commodities and Bonds 
Crude Oil WTI -4.2% to $83.44/bbl. Gold -3.8% to $4,504.1/oz. Natural Gas +2.5% to 2.88. Ten-Year Bond Yield -0.2 bps to 4.722. 

 Forex and Cryptos 
EUR/USD -0.82% . USD/JPY +0.72% . GBP/USD -0.74% . Bitcoin +0.4% . Litecoin -6.3% . Ethereum +0.4% . XRP -5.5% . 

 Top S&P 500 Gainers 
Salesforce ( CRM ) +22% . CrowdStrike Holdings ( CRWD ) +14% . ServiceNow ( NOW ) +13% . Veeva Systems ( VEEV ) +12% . Synopsys ( SNPS ) +11% . 

 Top S&P 500 Losers 
PayPal Holdings ( PYPL ) -13% . Generac Holdings ( GNRC ) -11% . Hormel Foods ( HRL ) -10% . Casey's General Stores ( CASY ) -10% . Marvell Technology ( MRVL ) -9% .
